complaint: This cover is not right: one side slopes down neatly, the other side stays straight. The daybed is the same on the left and the right.
cause: The cover was built with an uneven set of panels: on the right side there is an angled panel (normal 0.82, -0.57, 0.06), while the left side uses a straight vertical panel (normal -1, 0, 0) and a separate top slope (normal -0.2, -0.37, 0.91). The furniture is left-right symmetric, but the cover's panels are not mirror images, so one side slopes and the other stays straight.
rule: For furniture that is left-right symmetric, the cover must be left-right symmetric: every panel on one side must have an identical mirrored panel on the other side.
check: Mirror each panel's centre and normal across the furniture's left-right centre plane and verify that a matching panel with the same area exists within a small tolerance.

complaint: The top can be cut in one piece (the owner, 2 Oct 2026); it was 4 pieces with a 3.7 cm sliver.
cause: The box with 7 pieces was chosen for a tighter fit; its top became four faces, one only 37 mm wide, although the whole top lies flat about 1.2 m wide and fits the 1.48 m roll.
rule: Choose the box option with the fewest top pieces that fit the roll; never an option with a piece narrower than the minimum piece width (a sliver); more room round the furniture is a fair price for a top without seams.
check: The audit's slivers check (no piece narrower than seams.min_piece_width_mm) and its top pieces note.

complaint: You drew a sloping side instead of an L shape with a sharp corner; when generating these big covers the cover must follow the product and not draw diagonal lines (the owner, 7 Oct 2026).
cause: The box cover is the intersection of flat half-spaces, so it is always convex: over a chaise longue and a 2-seater placed as an L, the face that took away the most room was a slanted wall across the open inner corner, and one top spanned the whole L (1.66 m in its narrowest direction, over the roll).
rule: A cover over furniture placed together follows the pieces seen from above: their rectangles joined, right-angled inner corners, every wall straight down, nothing spanning an open corner; tops slope down to each piece's own front and pieces wider than the roll are split with seams running downhill. One rectangle round everything, or the smoothed outline, only when chosen on the page.
check: The audit's plan check (the cover within the pieces plus the clearance, seen from above) and the tests in engine/tests/test_arrange.py (an L gives an L with a sharp inner corner).

complaint: Crossed-out panels can become one panel (Rens, 8 Oct 2026; also the bar chairs, Vittoria, the corners Aspen, Avero and Emar, Monte Vari, Sato).
cause: A flat top is drained into a gable of two faces at the minimum slope (a 10 degree fold) and the box's face choice adds near-parallel faces (3 to 7 degrees); every flat face was its own piece.
rule: Neighbouring box faces on the same side that meet at a fold of at most seams.fold_join_max_deg lie flat together: one piece with a fold line, the gentlest fold first, while it fits the roll.
check: The audit's gentle folds check and engine/tests/test_facets.py (a gable top is one piece).

complaint: For the cut pieces please follow the lines of the original model (Rens, 8 Oct 2026; also S60).
cause: A given cover surface got the usual level skirt seam and a roll split; its own creases (the top's front and back edges) were ignored.
rule: A cover surface of its own is cut along its own creases sharper than seams.given_crease_deg; the pieces are what the creases enclose.
check: engine/tests/test_given_creases.py (a given surface with creases is cut on them).

complaint: The right number of vents, but too many at the back, the side not seen on the drawing: per back panel move one vent to the front, at the circles; all at the same height on the skirt, in the middle of the panels (Rens, 8 Oct 2026, 49 covers).
cause: The drawing's vent count was spread over the sides by length, so the long back walls got two or three and the front walls of an L, U or C (skipped as inner walls) none; a free top edge counted as hem and got a vent upside down; a box cover's low band got no vents at all.
rule: Vents go round every side of the cover, the seen front too, including the front (inner) walls in the inner corner of an L, U or C (owner, 9 Oct 2026: yes; features.vent_inner_walls on): one in the middle of each piece first, a side not served yet before another piece facing the same way, extra ones on the longest pieces; the drawing's number kept; all at the bottom, never on a free top edge; a band too low for a vent hands it to the piece above.
check: The audit's vents check (count, every side served, inner walls included, none high up a wall) and scripts/fewer_check.py (accepts vents on inner walls when the cover's switch is on, the default).

complaint: Make the cover round in top view, not square or octagonal; follow the (round, organic) outline of the furniture from the top view better (Rens at the Desk, 8 Oct 2026, on 18 round tables and 12 lounges).
cause: The box cover is an intersection of flat half-spaces: its plan is a convex polygon of a few straight sides, so a round table (with the chair ring round it) got a square or an octagon, and a kidney- or moon-shaped sofa a polygon over empty floor and across its bays.
rule: A box cover's plan comes from the furniture seen from above: when the footprint fills at least hull.round_fill of its smallest circle the cover is a round skirt with a cone on top resting on the support (water runs off, the skirt seam level, the top in equal sectors that fit the roll); when the box's straight sides stand more than hull.plan_follow_mm beyond the outline, the walls stand straight down on the outline (bays and inner corners rounded to hull.plan_round_mm) under the box's own top faces, which still span seats.
check: The audit's outline check (a box built where round or follow is due fails) and engine/tests/test_outline.py (a round table gets a round cover, a kidney sofa keeps its bay).

complaint: The marked part is empty space, make the cover smaller (Rens at the Desk, 8 Oct 2026, on six dining chairs).
cause: The word 'dining' in a chair's name made it a dining table: chair space (33 cm deep, 87 cm high) was added in front of and behind the chair, so the cover was twice as deep as the chair.
rule: Chair space only round a table: never round furniture named chair, stool, sofa or bench, and only when the table's top is at least hull.table_top_min_mm deep both ways (a chair's highest part is a backrest rail).

complaint: The outline of the generated cover does not match the drawing at all (Rens, 9 Oct 2026, QUESTIONS 4); also S20, S38/S39, S48, S25 rejected on shape.
cause: Drawings were read as one familiar block (a box, an L, a slope across the width) instead of view by view: D5 is a rectangle with a half round of the full width centred where the straight sides end, one slope from the strip over the round front, ends that lean in; S38/S39 have a front corner lower than the other (the top tilts two ways); S20/S48 have arms with a seat between them.
rule: Read every written size and check that the shape gives each one back (D5: 193.99, 177.98, 195.32 at 110.22 and 62.35 all come out of one hip shape). A round front with no height of its own follows the slope (hip free edges). Arms are followed and the seat between them is one panel falling to its front edge (rule 12). Heights are read per corner, not one front height.
check: engine/tests/test_drawing_given.py (free round front, arms with a spanned seat, a slanted front wall); every drawing_shape.json builds and fits the roll.

complaint: The top panel (1.85 m) does not fit the 1.48 m roll: split the panel (Rens at the Desk, 9 Oct 2026, question 16).
cause: Only the arrangements' and the follow covers' tops were cut into strips when wider than the roll; a plain (convex) box cover kept a too-wide top face as one piece and only reported it.
rule: Every box cover's top face wider than the roll is cut across its slope into strips whose seams run downhill (hull.json box.roll_cuts), after the gentle-fold joins, so no piece is wider than the roll.
check: scripts/fewer_check.py and the audit's pieces check (a piece wider than the roll fails); engine/tests/test_answers_box.py::test_a_box_top_wider_than_the_roll_is_cut_in_strips.

complaint: Follow the top view; at the side a chamfer instead of a bulge (Rens, 9 Oct 2026, question 3); a gentle gable on a follow cover was two pieces.
cause: A follow cover (ADR-107) kept every top face as a piece: the gentle-fold join of ADR-099 ran only on convex box covers, and the audit took a curved wall's own facets for gentle folds.
rule: A follow cover's flat top faces at a fold of at most seams.fold_join_max_deg are one piece with a fold line, as on any box cover; its curved walls keep their seams. A chamfer the approver asks for is a face added by hand (hull.box_extra_faces), never a curved cover.
check: The audit's gentle folds check (curved pieces left out); engine/tests/test_answers_box.py.

complaint: For covers with an organic shape like S53 and S60, which have curved seams, follow the drawing; not for all covers (Rens, 9 Oct 2026, question 19).
cause: ADR-100 made the cover model's own creases the seams for every given cover surface (seams.given_crease_deg 20 as the company default).
rule: Creases as seams only for organic covers: seams.given_crease_deg is 0 by default and 20 in the family preset 'organic' (config/presets/organic.yaml); a cover joins it with "family": "organic".

complaint: Crossed-out panels reduced to one panel (Rens, Desk 9 Oct 2026, D1 and D2; the owner: 'some faces are still split'): the front wall was cut at the 18 cm skirt line though it is one flat face on the drawing's front view.
cause: skirt_cm in the person-read shape cut every upright wall at one height, also walls that run on in the same plane above the line.
rule: A drawing cover's flat wall that the drawing draws in one piece is one piece; the level skirt seam only where the wall meets a face in another direction. The struck-through pieces of a level back strip are one piece when it fits the roll (S32, strip_whole).
check: cover audit 'gentle folds' on given covers (seams.flat_split_max_deg); engine/tests/test_facets.py::test_the_audit_finds_a_flat_wall_split_on_a_drawing_cover, engine/tests/test_drawing_given.py::test_a_flat_wall_drawn_in_one_piece_is_one_piece.

complaint: The main size 343.6 cm must be 344 cm (C4), 356 cm must be 357 cm (C8), the cover 357 x 357 cm with skirt right and skirt front both 92 cm (C10); the side and back skirts of S33 and C29 not equal to each other and not as drawn (Rens at the Desk, 9 Oct 2026).
cause: A cover fitted to the drawing's 3D view (isofit, ADR-094) took its footprint from the traced top view: each edge a few mm off its written size and a hair out of square, so mirror-equal walls differed (91.6 / 92.1 cm). Inch values converted (111.00 in = 281.9 cm) stood beside the drawing's own '282 cm', and the order number ('cover 86') was read as a size.
rule: The top view is made true to the drawing's written sizes before the heights are fitted: every outline edge near a written size is exactly that size (the drawing's own cm value, never our measured or inch-converted one), edges near square are square, and on a mirror-symmetric outline mirror-equal edges are one size (the larger, when the drawing writes them at most drawing.isofit_same_cm apart; written further apart they stay as written).
check: The audit's 'written sizes' check (a fitted top view's back lengths off their written size fail); engine/tests/test_drawing_isofit.py::test_the_traced_top_view_is_made_true_to_the_written_sizes and ::test_mirror_edges_written_a_hair_apart_are_one_size_written_far_apart_stay; engine/tests/test_drawing_views.py::test_the_drawings_own_cm_value_wins_over_an_inch_value_beside_it.

complaint: No vents on rounded corners, otherwise a fine cover (Rens at the Desk, 9 Oct 2026, the Casto daybed).
cause: Each piece's vents sit at the middles of equal shares of its bottom edge; a skirt piece that wraps a rounded corner of the plan (follow covers, box covers with rounded corners) got a vent on the bend.
rule: No vent on a rounded corner (features.vent_on_corners false): a vent whose bottom edge, with features.vent_seam_clearance_mm either side, turns more than features.vent_corner_max_deg in plan moves along its piece to the nearest straight stretch, clear of the piece's other vents; a piece round all along (a round cover) keeps its vents; places set by a person (features.vent_positions) are kept.
check: The audit's vents check ('on a rounded corner') and engine/tests/test_finish.py::test_no_vent_on_a_rounded_corner.

complaint: Back less tight, may be one continuous curve, smoother (Rens, 9 Oct 2026, both Pico covers); answered 14 Oct (QUESTIONS 101): the back wall plus the two back corners as one roomy arc from above, a few cm looser round the cushions, no kink at the corners.
cause: A follow plan keeps the furniture's outline plus the clearance; where a back cushion stands out near a back corner the outline has a 1-2 cm dent and a tight corner.
rule: On request per model (hull.plan_back_arc): behind the plan's widest points the outline is filled out to its convex hull, grown by hull.plan_back_ease_mm and its corners rounded (hull.plan_back_round_mm); the side walls lean out over hull.plan_back_taper_mm. When a reviewer asks for a smoother or looser back on a sofa with a curved back, propose this.

complaint: On 4 BBQ covers with side tables one vent does not fit where the rule wants it (owner, 12 Oct 2026, QUESTIONS 81: one vent fewer on that side, the rest by the rule).
cause: A kamado's handle stands in front of the side tables; the box's plan gets a 24-25 cm strip beside the front, shorter than a vent and its seam allowances.
rule: features.vent_short_piece_ok (on in presets/bbq): a piece too short for a vent simply has none and it is no warning; elsewhere it stays a warning.

complaint: The main sizes do not match the drawing (Rens at the Desk, 14 Oct 2026, C4, C8 and C10, after their plan sizes had been made exact).
cause: The size drawing (sizes.pdf) and the Sizes tab measured every height from hull.json's hem.height_mm, the hem parameter (5 cm). A drawing cover ends where the drawing ends, at the ground, so every height they showed was 5 cm short (84 cm drawn as 79, 31 as 26); the pieces, the 3D cover and the check list were right.
rule: Sizes are measured on the cover itself: heights from the lowest point of its own hem, never from a parameter. hull.json for a cover surface of its own records the lower edge as built. A size drawing of an older format is made again when it is opened.
check: The audit's 'written heights' check (an isofit drawing cover's shown height and arm-end height against the drawing's written back and end heights) and engine/tests/test_flatten.py::test_size_drawing_measures_from_the_covers_own_lower_edge.

complaint: The cover must simply be twice the panel on the drawing, the two stitched together all round except the bottom line (Rens at the Desk, 14 Oct 2026, U1 and U2, parasol covers).
cause: A drawing with one side view only was turned into a round cover (U2, ADR-102) or read as a sloped box (U1). The drawing draws the flat panel itself.
rule: A drawing of one flat outline alone, open at the bottom, is a flat bag: two equal panels of that outline, stitched together on every edge but the lowest line (drawing_given 'flat-bag'; the route-A side-view reader builds it too), no air vents.

complaint: Follow the seams better, as on the drawing (Rens at the Desk, 14 Oct 2026, S43 and S44).
cause: The swept builder ends the strip and the slope square across at the arc's end and puts the round nose beyond it; the drawing ends the strip on a slanted line, runs the back band on round the nose and the slope on to the nose's front. While building it, two arcs sampled at other angles left two pieces unjoined along 163 cm, and no check saw it.
rule: Seams of a drawing cover are where the drawing draws them, traced point by point when no builder makes them (scripts/s43_shape.py writes them as faces). Two pieces that touch but are not joined above the hem are an error.
check: The audit's 'open seams' check (free edges of two pieces in one place above the hem, from panels.npz) and engine/tests/test_drawing_given.py::test_s43_seams_as_drawn, ::test_the_audit_flags_two_pieces_left_unjoined.
